C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3.Summary:
One deliverable: the supersede replacement for `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` under `D27`. That bundle's output is committed at `74f706aa1f26d95687c2fb23fa179351dfde9e33` (branch `c-flush-and-pay`, this bundle's base) and `validate:ci` is green there — but defects were then found in the delivered suite itself, and two of them cannot be repaired inside `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` because its approved spec carries the hard Constraint that "the replacement relations are exactly the three in the repair Goal", and `D27` makes `ngrace supersede` the only repair route for an approved artifact. The maintainer has ruled: supersede. One deliverable file, `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, three repairs in one bundle (`D11`: nothing is deferred, and nothing needs to be — all three land here):
**R1 — the pairing loop is a zero-or-more-swallow.** The test "pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes" binds a node list per file and only iterates it; nothing requires the list to be non-empty, so the test is satisfied by zero elements (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:619` at this commit). Measured on a throwaway copy of the repository: with every `<Finding>` element in `findings.xml` renamed (210 elements, measured by the shipped parser over direct children), the suite still passes — 26 pass, 0 fail, exit 0, with 1589 expect() calls against the control's 2009. The repair is a non-vacuity assertion that carries no numeric literal, because the shipped anti-occupancy guard rejects any numeric literal inside that test's body, `0` included.
**R2 — the index relation contradicts the shipped engine.** The test derives the live index `Entry` set by `entry.attributes.layer === "live"` (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:657` at this commit); the shipped record engine derives it by `entry.attributes.layer !== "retired"` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:996`, the `liveEntryCount` metric at :991 that both the persist path at :1260 and the ceiling check at :1439 consume). The shipped validator never re-derives the persisted `base` against the metric (`checkCeilingValue` at :1514 compares only `liveSize > ceiling`), so the test relation is the only instrument comparing `base` to the live count — and on the discriminating record state (one direct `Entry` child carrying no `layer` attribute at all, `base` untouched) the engine metric includes it, every shipped validator accepts the record (`record-retirement: ok`, exit 0, driven on a throwaway copy), and the shipped test reds (270 filtered vs 271 base, driven). The criterion must hold the engine's predicate: the test's job is to be the canary over the engine's own invariant, and a stricter predicate contradicts the engine on a state the engine accepts and persists.
**R3 — the anti-occupancy guard is evadable, brittle, and hand-rolls a lexer.** Three measured failures, each on a throwaway copy, each reproduced before this spec was written: (a) *evasion* — a module-scope binding whose initializer holds its number behind an internal semicolon (`const SNEAKY = (() => { const setup = "x"; return 195; })();`) referenced from the guarded test's body as a count comparison: the pairing test reds (195 vs 271) and the regression guard stays green, because the initializer slice terminates at the first semicolon (`moduleBindingInitializer` at `src/artifact/xml.test.ts:900`) and never reaches the number; (b) *false red* — reformatting the pairing test's callback to `async () => {`: the pairing test still passes, and the guard fails the suite with "the pairing test's body span could not be located", because the hand-rolled span locator (`pairingBodySpan` at :724) matches only the exact `,\s*\(\)\s*=>\s*\{` shape; (c) *invisible bindings* — `MODULE_BINDING_SHAPE` (:681) sees neither a binding introduced by destructuring nor a second declarator in a single statement: with `const { DESTRUCTED_PIN } = { DESTRUCTED_PIN: 195 };` and `const FIRST_PIN = 195, SECOND_PIN = 195;` both referenced from the guarded body, the suite is fully green (26 pass, 0 fail, exit 0, driven). Meanwhile the file already imports and uses a real TypeScript parser — `import ts from "typescript"` at :5, consumed by `collectFromText` at :392 (`ts.createSourceFile` at :393), the structural-clone single-definition scanner — and the hand-rolled scanner (`scanCode` at :753 and the three shapes at :679-681) provides no capability that parser does not: the parser yields exact byte positions, classifies numeric literal nodes directly (subsuming the regex, which also misses exponent and hexadecimal forms), visits every declarator including destructured names, and spans initializers as expression nodes so internal statement boundaries cannot hide their contents. The replacement guard is chartered over that parser, keeping the shipped contract — keyed on the count forms, refusing what it cannot prove.
This spec overturns a clause of its predecessor deliberately, in the `Constraints`: the exactly-three clause is widened to admit R1's non-vacuity assertion and the R3 guard replacement, and the overturn answers the argument behind the clause. The predecessor's committed engine work stands untouched: this bundle writes no record file, edits no `scripts/` file, performs no supersede, and raises no ceiling. The record end state the predecessor asserted needs no re-assertion here: this bundle's base `74f706aa1f26d95687c2fb23fa179351dfde9e33` is the post-flush commit, and `AC-RECORD-UNTOUCHED` pins all seven record files byte-identically to it, which subsumes any semantic end-state claim for this window. Binding live rulings `D27` and `D27.1` (supersede is the route; this draft is corrected in place until ratified), `D11`, `D30` (dated figures in Assumptions, never in hard Constraints), `D28` and `D28.1` (the enforcement and ceilings asserted green and never changed), `F136.1` (one module enumeration). Name searched 2026-09-10 at this commit: no archive directory and no `Row` in either registry layer carries `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3`; the name is new.
C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3.Problem:
`C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` delivered a green suite at `74f706aa1f26d95687c2fb23fa179351dfde9e33` (`bun run validate:ci` exits 0 there; `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` reports 26 pass, 0 fail, exit 0 — both read directly at this commit). The defects below were then measured against the delivered test file. Each is a hole the delivered criteria let through, and two are unrepairable there because the approved spec's occupancy-prohibition Constraint fixes the replacement relations at exactly three and its `AC-NO-SRC-BEYOND-REPAIR` forbids any further change to the repair file; under `D27` the route is supersede, and this bundle is the replacement.
**The zero-or-more-swallow (R1).** The pairing test's per-file loop binds `childNodes(parsed.root!, tag)` (:619) and iterates it; every per-element assertion lives inside the loop, so an empty list satisfies the whole test vacuously. The suite cannot notice a record genre emptied of its elements: renaming every `<Finding>` element in `findings.xml` on a throwaway copy leaves the suite green (measured, tails in VerificationIntent), with the identity, pairing and disjointness assertions silently skipped — 420 fewer expect() calls and no failure. The relations catch duplication, copy-instead- -of-move and a wrongly flipped `Entry`; they catch nothing when the elements themselves are absent from the walk. The obvious repair — a greater-than-zero assertion — is itself refused by the shipped guard, which rejects any numeric literal inside the pairing test's body (`0` included), so the non-emptiness form must carry no digit.
**The contradictory index predicate (R2).** The shipped engine's `liveEntryCount` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:996`) counts direct `Entry` children whose `layer` attribute is not `retired` — an `Entry` carrying no `layer` attribute is live to the engine. The test (:657) counts only `layer === "live"` and compares that to the persisted `base`. On the discriminating record state — one `Entry`'s `layer` attribute removed, `base` left at 271 — the validator's ceiling check stays green (it compares only `liveSize > ceiling`, :1514, and never re-derives `base`), the persist path (:1260) would keep `base` at the engine's metric, and the shipped test fails with "Expected: 270, Received: 271". A shipped criterion that reds on a record state the shipped engine accepts, persists and validates is a defect of the criterion, not of the record: the predicate the test must hold is the engine's, so the canary measures the engine's own invariant rather than a stricter one nobody writes.
**The hand-rolled guard (R3).** The shipped regression guard is a hand-rolled lexer over the file's own source: `scanCode` (:753) blanks comments, strings and template contents with a character walk, `pairingBodySpan` (:724) locates the pairing test's body by matching a fixed open-argument shape after the title needle, `moduleBindingInitializer` (:900) slices a binding's initializer to its first terminating semicolon, and three regex shapes (:679-681) carry the count forms. Measured: it is silent on a restored occupancy pin whose number sits behind an internal semicolon in the initializer (R3-a); it fails the suite on a cosmetic `async` reformat of the callback (R3-b); it cannot see a destructured numeric binding or a non-first declarator referenced from the guarded body (R3-c). The file already carries the TypeScript parser and uses it for the structural-clone single-definition scan; the lexer is the weaker instrument, and its replacement over the parser is implementable today — the bar (silent on R3's second probe, red on its first and third, the suite's synthetic directions green at close) is demonstrated driven on throwaway copies with a working prototype of exactly this shape (tails in VerificationIntent).
The predecessor cannot carry these repairs: its approved spec binds the replacement relations at exactly three and forbids further writes to the one file all three repairs live in. The authority supersedes `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` once this spec exists; this bundle performs no outward-facing act itself.

Goals.Goal: **R1 — the pairing walk is never vacuous.** In `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, the test "pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes" asserts, without any numeric literal, that every paired genre child list is non-empty. The chartered form, proven green on the real record and red on a hollowed copy in both directions before this spec was written: destructure the first element of the bound node list and require it defined — `const [firstGenreChild] = nodes;` then `expect(firstGenreChild, ...).toBeDefined();` — a form that carries no digit, so the shipped guard's numeric-literal scan over the body stays green on it. Red direction: hollow one record genre on a throwaway copy of the repository (rename every `<Finding>` element of `findings.xml` to some other tag, root attributes and close tag untouched) and run the suite inside the copy — the repaired test exits 1 naming the genre's non-emptiness (driven: "findings.xml:Finding carries at least one element", Received: undefined). Green direction: the real record (driven: 33 pass, 0 fail, exit 0 in the prototype state carrying all three repairs). The assertion adds no count: it asserts existence, reads nothing transcribed, and expires under no legitimate write.

**R2 — the index relation holds the engine's predicate.** In the same test, the index-bookkeeping relation derives the live `Entry` set with exactly the shipped engine's predicate — every direct `Entry` child whose `layer` attribute is not `retired` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:996`), the metric the engine's persist path (:1260) and ceiling check (:1439) both consume — so the persisted `base` is compared against exactly the count the engine defines and writes, with no stricter and no looser predicate. The discriminating record state (one direct `Entry` child carrying no `layer` attribute, `base` untouched) is accepted by the shipped validator and green under the repaired predicate, where the shipped test reds; the repaired relation's own red direction is the dropped-entry mutation — remove one live `Entry` without re-persisting `base`, and the repaired test reds (270 vs 271, driven) while the shipped validator stays silent (driven: `record-retirement: ok`), because it never re-derives the persisted base against the metric. The engine is the standard here, not a surface: this bundle edits no engine file and widens no metric.

**R3 — the guard over the real parser.** The anti-occupancy guard is reimplemented over the TypeScript parser the file already imports and uses, and the hand-rolled scanner is gone: `scanCode`, `pairingBodySpan`, `moduleBindingInitializer` and the three regex shapes at :679-681 are removed with their lexer. The replacement keeps the shipped contract — keyed on the count forms, binding on the pairing test's body shape, refusing what it cannot prove — and carries the same three detection duties, widened to close the measured failures: (1) any numeric literal inside the pairing test's callback body, read from the parser's numeric-literal nodes, so string and comment prose cannot fire and exponent, hexadecimal and separator forms are seen; (2) the occupancy-table field shape anywhere in the file — a member named `expected` typed `number`, in interface/type-literal form and labeled-tuple form (`Array<[file: string, expected: number]>`, the shape the predecessor's table actually carried), while the same prose inside a string literal is not a hit; (3) any module-scope binding with a numeric initializer referenced from the body — every declarator of a module-scope variable statement visited, destructured names and non-first declarators included, and the initializer examined in full as an expression node, so a number behind an internal semicolon or brace is seen. The bar, binding on the plan and machine-observed at close by the shipped synthetic directions: the R3-a probe is red (the SNEAKY-shaped initializer is caught), the R3-b probe is green (an `async` callback reformats without a false red, the timeout argument outside the body never firing), the R3-c probe is red (both binding forms caught), and when the pairing test's callback cannot be located the guard reports its refusal rather than passing. The suite ships these directions as synthetic self-tests beside the real-file direction, so every clause is exercised by the close's own suite run. Known boundary, stated rather than hidden: an identifier occurrence in the body — a property name included — counts as a reference (over-approximate, never under), and a locally shadowed name is not distinguished from an outer binding, the shipped word-boundary behavior retained.

**The supersede window, and what this bundle does not perform.** The authority supersedes `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2` once this spec exists — an outward-facing act under `D27` that this spec requests but does not perform. The move edits only the predecessor bundle's paths under `.ngrace/changes/`, writes no record file, and mints no eligibility: no `Row` in either registry layer carries the name `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3` (searched at this commit), and no `Row` carries the predecessor's name either, so the close ceremony's move is a no-op (`F196`'s post-close rule, inherited). Every byte-invariance criterion below therefore holds in the only state where `CloseEvidence` is ever evaluated, and each exclusion that keeps it satisfiable is named with its reason in the criterion.

Constraints.Constraint:
Ceremony tier T1: one `src/` test file, this bundle's own artifacts; no record write, no `scripts/` edit, no runtime file of any graph module edited. Roadmap: RM-GOVERNED-PATH (record integrity). Binding live rulings: `D27` and `D27.1` (supersede is the only repair route for the approved predecessor; this spec is a draft and is corrected in place until the maintainer ratifies it), `D11` (all three repairs land in this bundle; no follow-up bundle for any of them), `D30` (a spec may not pin scalar counts of a file it changes into its hard Constraints — what is forbidden is a Constraint whose truth expires the next time anyone writes the file; every dated figure in this spec lives in Assumptions and expires; the extension of that reasoning to test assertions over the record is this repository's convention, not `D30`'s text, and this bundle inherits it as shipped by its predecessor), `D28` and `D28.1` (the enforcement and ceilings this bundle asserts green and never revisits — no ceiling is raised, no eligibility scan or metric constant changed). `D30` scoped: this bundle writes no record file, so no freeze question arises; its hard Constraints transcribe no scalar count of any file it changes.
**Overturned clause, named and answered.** `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2`'s occupancy-prohibition Constraint states: "the replacement relations are exactly the three in the repair Goal; the anti-occupancy guard assertion ships in the same file, in the house body-shaped single-definition form, so the prohibition is machine-observed at close and not a prose promise." This spec deliberately widens that clause in two ways. First, the pairing test gains a fourth assertion beside the three relations: the non-vacuity requirement of R1 — not a relation between record layers and not a count, but the precondition without which the three relations are satisfiable by an empty record. The clause's argument was that a fixed, small relation set prevents occupancy pins from returning disguised as relations and keeps the replacement minimal; the non-vacuity assertion serves that same argument — it strengthens the corruption coverage the relations were chartered for, carries no number, and cannot expire under any legitimate write — so the widening answers the argument instead of reopening it. Second, the guard's implementation is replaced (R3): the clause's operative requirement — machine-observed at close, body-shaped, single-definition, never a prose promise — is preserved verbatim; only the detection mechanism is chartered over the TypeScript parser the file already imports, because the shipped lexer provably fails the bar the clause was written for. Nothing else about the predecessor's prohibition is widened: the prohibition itself (no transcribed record element count in any form) is inherited unchanged.

F136.1 anchors — files this spec forces into write scope, with their `LINKS:` state, listed here once and not repeated as a second module list anywhere: `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` — no contract header, re-checked at this commit; it is the test surface of the module whose runtime file is `src/artifact/xml.ts` and carries that module's `LINKS:` header (`M-GRAMMAR`, re-read at this commit); and this bundle's own artifacts under `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3/`. The module enumeration for this bundle is exactly: `M-GRAMMAR` (via `src/artifact/xml.ts`'s `LINKS:` header). No other graph module is written; do not mint a synthetic module; do not repeat this enumeration as a second module list. The record files under `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/`, the record engine `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` and its test, and every README, docs, skills and packaging surface are read, never written.

The occupancy prohibition, binding on the plan, inherited and amended. The repaired test must not carry a transcribed element count of any record file in any form — the `expected` column, a constant, or an inline literal compared against a parsed element count — and every number the test uses about a record file is read back from that file at test time. The chartered assertions are the predecessor's three relations with relation (c) re-derived under the engine's predicate, plus R1's non-vacuity assertion in a digit-free form; the anti-occupancy guard ships in the same file, in the house body-shaped single-definition form, implemented over the TypeScript parser the file already imports (`import ts from "typescript"`, consumed today by `collectFromText`), with the hand-rolled scanner removed (`scanCode`, `pairingBodySpan`, `moduleBindingInitializer`, and the three regex shapes), the refusal clause kept, and the guard's discriminating directions shipped as synthetic self-tests in the same suite. The plan observes the lexer's removal with a target assertion over `src/artifact/xml.test.ts` (for example `MustNotContain` over the shipped function names), so the implementation clause is machine-checked and not a prose promise. AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PAIRING-NONEMPTY:
The pairing test never passes on an emptied genre: the test "pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes" asserts, for every one of the seven record files, that the bound genre child list it walks is non-empty, in a form carrying no numeric literal (the chartered form: destructure the first element and require it defined), so the anti-occupancy guard's numeric-literal scan over the body stays green on it. The test keeps all of its other substance unchanged at this criterion's granularity: all seven real record files parsed at their committed bytes, non-null roots, `computeElementSpans` succeeding, identity completeness and within-file uniqueness, cross-layer disjointness, the index bookkeeping relation, and index `Entry` elements self-closing. Content question, answered by the shipped suite itself: the `CloseEvidence` runs the repaired suite, so the real-record green direction and the guard's green-on- the-body claim are machine-observed at close. Failure: the non-emptiness assertion is absent, weakened to a subset of the files, or reintroduces a numeric literal or a transcribed count. Mutations that redden the evidence, each on a throwaway copy of the repository with the copy's record mutated and the repaired suite run inside the copy (the pairing test resolves the record from its own tree and takes no path): rename every `<Finding>` element of `findings.xml` to some other tag — the repaired test exits 1 naming the file's non-emptiness (driven at this commit in the prototype state carrying the chartered form: 32 pass, 1 fail, the failure "findings.xml:Finding carries at least one element"), while the unmutated copy is green. The unmutated direction and the hollowed direction are both demonstrated by the later plan on throwaway copies before the artifact is approved.

The discriminating mutation, on a throwaway copy of the repository with the copy's record mutated and the repaired suite run inside the copy: remove one direct `Entry` child carrying `layer="live"` without re-persisting the roots — the repaired test exits 1 on the `base` read-back (driven at this commit: Expected 270, Received 271) while the shipped validator stays silent because it never re-derives the persisted base against the metric (driven at this commit: `record-retirement: ok`, exit 0); and the predecessor's discriminating state — one `Entry` carrying no `layer` attribute at all, `base` untouched — is accepted by the shipped validator (driven: `record-retirement: ok`) and green under the repaired predicate (driven: suite 33 pass, 0 fail) where the shipped predicate reds (driven: Expected 270, Received 271), which is the disagreement this repair removes. Both directions are demonstrated by the later plan on throwaway copies before the artifact is approved.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-GUARD-OVER-PARSER:
The anti-occupancy guard is shipped over the TypeScript parser and meets the bar. In `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`: the guard is implemented over the parser the file already imports (`import ts from "typescript"` — consumed in the shipped file by the structural-clone scanner, and after this bundle by the guard too), the hand-rolled scanner is gone (`scanCode`, `pairingBodySpan`, `moduleBindingInitializer`, and the `NUMERIC_LITERAL_SHAPE`, `OCCUPANCY_TABLE_SHAPE`, `MODULE_BINDING_SHAPE` shapes removed; the plan observes the removal with a target assertion over the file), the refusal clause is kept (an unlocatable pairing callback is reported, never passed), and the guard's three detection duties hold in their widened forms: numeric literals inside the pairing test's body (read from the parser's numeric-literal nodes, so string and comment prose never fires and the timeout argument outside the body never fires), the occupancy-table field shape anywhere in the file in interface/type-literal form and labeled-tuple form while its prose mention inside a string is not a hit, and module-scope bindings with numeric initializers referenced from the body with every declarator visited — destructured names and non-first declarators included — and the initializer examined in full, so a number behind an internal semicolon is seen. The suite ships the guard's discriminating directions as synthetic self-tests, all green at close: green on a pairing body with no numeric literals and no numeric bindings; red on an inline numeric literal in the body; red on a numeric initializer behind an internal semicolon (the R3-a shape) referenced from the body; red on a destructured numeric binding and on a non-first-declarator numeric binding referenced from the body, and not red on the same statement's unreferenced declarator; red on the occupancy-table shape in both forms and not red on its prose mention; green on an `async` callback; and the refusal message when the callback cannot be located. Content question, answered by the shipped suite itself: the `CloseEvidence` runs the suite, so every synthetic direction and the real-file direction (the shipped file's own body carries no count forms) are machine-observed at close. Failure: any synthetic direction is missing, weakened, or disagrees; the hand-rolled scanner survives; the guard passes instead of refusing when it cannot locate the pairing test. The real-copy probes are demonstrated by the later plan on throwaway copies of the repository before the artifact is approved, against the delivered file: the R3-a shape (`const SNEAKY = (() => { const setup = "x"; return 195; })();` referenced from the body) leaves the regression guard red with the numeric-initializer finding (driven at this commit against the prototype guard); the R3-b reformat (`async () => {`) leaves the whole suite green (driven: 33 pass, 0 fail); the R3-c bindings (destructured and non-first declarator, referenced from the body) leave the regression guard red naming both bindings (driven).
